notes: Event rules register what an input reports as having happened. They read the input directly and never enter the evidence pipeline: an event record never becomes an EvidenceSpan, carries no weight and produces no verdict. A record says which bounded family the event belongs to, whose act or state it is, the verbatim words it was read from, and why this release cannot sign a conclusion on it alone (commitment_reason). Everything a rule does not recognise stays silent: a missing record is a gap, an invented one puts words in somebody's mouth.

rules.notes: A declared state change, reported by the reader. It is a state report, not an act of courtship, so it never counts as an offer and never carries evidence weight on its own.

rules.notes: The friend-zone family, whose phrasings PR-0 showed were treated inconsistently: one wording reached the boundary rule, another was read as the reader's own discount, a third was never heard. Registering all of them here gives the family one material kind and one reason, without deciding that any of them is her boundary.

(家里|双方父母|两家人|长辈)(们)?(都)?(不同意|不赞成|不支持|反对|不希望|不看好)[^。！？!?，,]{0,6}(在一起|交往|谈恋爱|处对象|结婚|来往|走太近|走得太近|发展|继续)?
rules.notes: Somebody else objects to the relationship. This is resistance, not her boundary: the family records who objects and quotes the words, and PR-1's polarity layer already makes sure it is never offered as positive evidence. Registering it here is what stops the reader being told that nothing was heard. PR-6R1 widened the frame to the spoken form ("她室友说不希望我们走太近") and to the tail-less one ("但她妈妈不同意"), and put the whole rule behind a relationship-context requirement so the same words in a message about something else ("我妈不同意我换工作") stay silent.

Her answer denies that there is anything to read in the situation. Registered as a speech act the reader reported, with no commitment about what it means; the reader can see NED heard the answer rather than the silence.
